task.description:
WF-03 Step 4c -- RUN THE FULL SUITE and report. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821.

WHAT THIS RUN SHIPPED: a new test-only module test/support/tenant_fixture.ex
(Letflow.TenantFixture), its adoption in exactly two modules
(test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs, promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs), and 14 new
regression tests at test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs. NO production code changed.

RUN:
1. The full suite: `mix test`. It currently takes ~600s -- budget for it, do not substitute a
   subset. Report the real totals and the real duration.
2. The three run-relevant files in isolation as a separate run: the new test file plus the two
   adopted modules. Expected 14 + 8 + 12; report what you actually get.

ATTRIBUTION IS THE HARD PART OF THIS STEP, AND THERE IS A SPECIFIC TRAP. This suite has a
KNOWN environmental failure set -- the ISS-0048/0050/0060/0062/0064/0108 family, typically
~10 in Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest via restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0, plus
ExUnit.TimeoutError in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest. THE TRAP: the previous run
(WF02-REQ066-20260820) established that this set is LOAD-DEPENDENT, NOT a fixed list --
TEST-RUNNER got 14 failures and RELEASE-VALIDATOR got 15 on the same commit range twelve
minutes apart, and the difference was NOT noise: IdentityMigrationTest was stable at 10 both
times, Check.TestTest went 2->3, the two Promotion* failures that became ISS-0109 did NOT
recur, and two IdentityTest failures appeared that no issue covered (now ISS-0108/GH#360).
So: DO NOT attribute a failure to "the known environmental set" by module name or by count.
Match each failure individually -- module, test name, error class, and the specific assertion
-- against the recorded baselines in test/reports/ (report-20260820-WF02-REQ066-20260820.yaml
and report-20260819-WF02-REQ109-20260819.yaml). Any failure you cannot match that way is
UNATTRIBUTED, and saying so is the correct answer; guessing is not.

FOR EVERY FAILURE, state explicitly: caused by this branch, or pre-existing? The structural
evidence available to you: this branch changes no production code at all, so a failure in a
module that does not use Letflow.TenantFixture cannot be caused by it. Use `git diff
--stat main...HEAD` to establish the actual change surface rather than assuming it.

PAY PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO THE TWO MODULES THIS RUN TOUCHED. Letflow.Definitions.PromotionTest
and Letflow.Definitions.PromotionAssertionRerunTest are the modules ISS-0109 was filed about.
If either fails in the full-suite run, that is the highest-value observation this step can
produce and it must NOT be waved through as environmental: it would be either (a) a genuine
recurrence of the ISS-0109 symptom -- in which case the new fixture's capture and its
LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE log lines should now make it ATTRIBUTABLE, which is the entire point of
this run, so CAPTURE THAT OUTPUT IN FULL and quote it; or (b) a regression introduced by the
adoption. Distinguish them and say which.

ALSO CHECK, since the whole run exists to make a failure legible: grep the full-suite output
for the literal marker LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE and report what phases appear and how many. Under
a clean run you should see only phase=teardown lines, one per fixture call site across the two
adopted modules (19 sites were counted at implementation). A phase=provision_failed,
phase=replay_failed or phase=incomplete_schema line appearing anywhere is a real finding worth
the whole run.

WRITE the structured report to test/reports/report-<YYYYMMDD>-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml, matching the schema
the existing reports in that directory already use (read one first -- do not invent a shape).

DO NOT FIX ANYTHING. If a failure is attributable to this branch, report it as FAIL and ORCH
routes rework. If you discover an unrelated defect, report it in result.issues for ORCH to file
per ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- do not expand this run.

TOOLCHAIN: plain `mix test`. Do NOT run `mix format --check-formatted` or `mix compile
--warnings-as-errors` -- both fail on main itself under this host's Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against
a 1.18.3-otp-27 pin (ISS-0106/GH#354, filed, not yours), and a red gate you did not cause is not
this step's verdict. `mix` may not be on PATH bare; use "/c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix" quoted.
Postgres for this workspace is letflow-2-postgres-1 on LETFLOW_DB_PORT from ./.env -- do NOT run
`docker compose up` (see docs/anti-patterns.md; the container is already running and a second one
would collide with the sibling workspace).

Commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`. handoffs/orchestrator.log is ORCH's -- leave it
alone, and `git fetch` rather than pulling if a rebase refuses.
acceptance_criteria: The full `mix test` suite was run on this branch and real totals plus real duration are quoted
The three run-relevant files were also run in isolation, with actual counts reported

Every failure is attributed INDIVIDUALLY -- module, test name, error class and assertion matched against the recorded baselines in test/reports/ -- not by module name or by count against 'the known environmental set'; anything unmatchable is reported as UNATTRIBUTED
Each failure carries an explicit caused-by-this-branch vs pre-existing verdict, with the change surface established from git diff --stat main...HEAD rather than assumed

Letflow.Definitions.PromotionTest and Letflow.Definitions.PromotionAssertionRerunTest are specifically addressed: either they passed, or the failure is diagnosed as ISS-0109 recurrence (with the new capture/log output quoted in full) or as an adoption regression
The full-suite output was grepped for the literal LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker and the phases found are reported with counts
A structured report exists at test/reports/report-<YYYYMMDD>-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml matching the schema of the existing reports in that directory
Nothing was fixed; any unrelated defect is reported in result.issues rather than repaired

result.summary: Full mix test on feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821 (commit 12286e8, seed 993324): 1228/1244 passed (5/5 properties, 1223/1239 tests), 16 failed, 612.1s reported / 614s wall (02:54:34Z-03:04:48Z), exit 2. Isolation run of the three run-relevant files (seed 137760): Result: 34 passed, exit 0, 27.1s -- exactly the predicted 14 + 8 + 12. ZERO of the 16 failures are caused by this branch: git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- lib/ priv/ config/ mix.exs returns only a markdown design doc, so no production code changed, and none of the five failing modules references Letflow.TenantFixture (grep verified). Attribution was done per-failure on four axes (module, test name, error class, assertion/frame) against the two recorded test/reports/ baselines, never by module name or count: 12 ATTRIBUTED (10 IdentityMigrationTest 23503 FK violation at restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0:242, all ten test names matching the baseline list; 2 Check.TestTest ExUnit.TimeoutError at collect/2:110 lines 105/126), 1 ATTRIBUTED BY CLASS ONLY (Check.TestTest third test at line 147 -- same module, error class and frame, but this test is in neither test/reports/ baseline; corroborated by ISS-0108 cross_run_variance and ISS-0107 but not baseline-matched), and 3 UNATTRIBUTED (Letflow.EngineConcurrencyTest 42P01 on instance_projections; Letflow.Definitions.RollbackTest 3F000 invalid_schema_name; Letflow.IdentityTest 42P01 on a per-tenant users table). PROMOTION VERDICT: Letflow.Definitions.PromotionTest and Letflow.Definitions.PromotionAssertionRerunTest both PASSED -- absent from all 16 failure headers and green in isolation (8/8 and 12/12). No ISS-0109 recurrence in them and no adoption regression. HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING: the ISS-0109 signature reproduced verbatim in Letflow.Definitions.RollbackTest -- same 3F000 invalid_schema_name, same {:error, {:migration_failed, %MatchError{...}}} wrapper, same failing assertion on TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1, raised from that module OWN hand-rolled provisioned_tenant/0 at rollback_test.exs:120 -- i.e. the condition surfaced in a module that has NOT adopted the fixture while both adopted modules stayed green. MARKER AUDIT: 29 LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE lines -- 25 phase=teardown (19 from the two adopted modules, exactly the 19 implementation-counted call sites: 8 req037-promo + 11 req040-assertion-rerun; 6 from the fixture own test file) and 4 phase=incomplete_schema, all four deliberately induced by broken_state_tenant!/1 (slugs iss0109-c1b/-c2a/-c2b/-c3) in regression tests that PASSED. Zero phase=provision_failed, zero phase=replay_failed. Nothing was fixed. Gates mix format --check-formatted and --warnings-as-errors were not run, per the handoff (ISS-0106/GH#354 fails on main). Postgres: existing letflow-2-postgres-1 on port 5472; docker compose up was NOT run; 0 too_many_connections in the log.
